extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural grantee organizations, institutional officials (SOs/AOs), extramural administrators, account administrators, principal investigators, IAR/FSR users
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and constraints for registering institutions, creating and managing user accounts and affiliations, maintaining institution and personal profiles, verifying PI support, and querying/viewing grant and progress-report status within the NIH eRA Commons web system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Username requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The User Name (username) must be a unique name with a minimum of 6 characters and a maximum of 20 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User Name fields have a 6-character minimum and a 20-character maximum. The username must be unique and can be any combination of letters and numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Passwords must be at least 6 characters long and are case-sensitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When changing password the new password must be different than the current password. Passwords are case-sensitive. The system generates a new password when resetting and prompts the user to change it on first use.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-time login password change
rubrics_metrics.description: On first login the user is required to change the system-provided password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this is the first time logging in, the Change Password page opens. Enter the old password and then enter and retype a new password; click Submit to update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password reset process
rubrics_metrics.description: Users who forget their password can request a password reset which generates a system password sent to the email on file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the Login page click 'Forgot Password?' and provide User ID and registered email. The new system-generated password is emailed to the registered address; on first logon with the generated password the user is prompted to change it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password expiration and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: User passwords expire for security and the system notifies users when their password is close to expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If password is about to expire a 'password close to expiration' message appears at login. When the password expires the user is directed to select a new password; no notification to others is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web browser and client settings
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH eRA Commons requires a supported web browser and certain client settings for full functionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended browsers include Internet Explorer 5.01 or greater or Netscape 4.7 or greater. Cookies and JavaScript must be enabled. Use system navigation buttons/links rather than browser back/forward buttons. Do not use automatic password completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Session expiration policy
rubrics_metrics.description: User sessions expire after 45 minutes of inactivity with a five-minute warning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five minutes before expiration an expiration message appears offering 'Keep Session' or 'Abandon Session'. If session expires and pages exhibit errors (missing buttons, Internal Server Error 500, pages with no data), close the browser and start a new session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent login policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A user may have only one active NIH eRA Commons session at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a second login attempt occurs, the system offers to terminate the first session or cancel the new login attempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing pages
rubrics_metrics.description: All eRA Commons pages can be printed using the browser's print feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printing is useful to provide a hard-copy report of what you see on screen; use the browser's standard print feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the demo/training facility
rubrics_metrics.description: A demo mode allows users to practice creating sample institutions, accounts, and grant applications using sample data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access via Commons—Demo link. Use Create a New Demo Account form to create sample institution and accounts. All fields on the demo account form are required. The demo requires creation of an SO account; created PI accounts may be assigned sample grants. First-time login requires password change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution registration - authorized registrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Only authorized organization officials can register grantee institutions in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your Office of Sponsored Programs or Office of Clinical Research representative for information on who may register; the registration process creates a mandatory Signing Official (SO) account and optional Accounts Administrator (AA) account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution registration - required fields and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain registration fields are required and have length/format constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields with an asterisk (*) are required. At least one line of street address (Street 1) is required. Institution Name has a 100-character maximum. Title field for SO can contain up to 240 characters. User Name must be at least 6 characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution registration - signed form and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing online registration, the registration form must be printed, signed by an SO or designee, and faxed to NIH; the SO must verify email via hyperlink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the online form to generate a registration form with signature/date lines; fax the completed signed form to NIH (number provided). NIH sends an email to the designated SO containing a hyperlink to verify the SO email address; NIH will review and approve the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirming institution registration and conflict handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution registration confirmation checks for conflicts with NIH's existing name and address information and provides overwrite or correction options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After SO email confirmation and NIH review, a second email provides a hyperlink to confirm and complete registration; if name/address conflicts occur options are given to change or overwrite NIH on-file data. Institution names and addresses can be manually updated later via Edit Institution Profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating user accounts - two methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Extramural Administrators can create new user accounts either by matching to existing NIH eRA user profiles (recommended for PIs) or by directly creating new accounts for users without existing profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Create Account hyperlink when the user is a PI with an NIH eRA user profile to associate to existing records. Use the Create Account page when unable to query a desired account or for roles other than PI and IAR that don't have existing profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI account matching requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To associate a new PI account with an existing NIH PI profile, optional fields (birth date, SSN, prior support) should be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It's important that PIs with prior NIH support enter birth date, SSN, and prior support information to enable NIH to associate the new account to the PI's existing NIH profile and avoid duplicate accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create Account field constraints and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Create Account requires certain fields and enforces username uniqueness and length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required fields are indicated with an asterisk. The User Name field must be unique and have 6-20 characters. For PI roles, Birth Date, SSN, and Prior Support fields are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications and activation for new accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: After account creation, the new user receives an email with username and a randomly generated password (except PIs require confirmation first).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New users receive 'Account Created' notification email sent to the provided email with credentials. New PI accounts receive an email with a link to a special form to confirm NIH information; only after PI confirmation does the PI receive account info. Pending NIH verification typically lasts 2–3 business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Querying accounts - optional fields and matching rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Account queries can use optional fields; User ID, Last Name, and First Name fields support partial, case-insensitive matches. Roles can be multi-selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select Administration | Accounts | Maintain Account to query. Use any combination of fields. Press Ctrl to select multiple roles. Up to 50 records display per page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account status definitions and actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Account statuses include Not Affiliated, Pending, Active, and All; each has specific meanings and available actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not Affiliated: users with submissions but not affiliated; Action column offers 'Create Account' or 'Create Affiliation'. Pending: user requested account and awaits validation; Status hyperlink available. Active: profile associated with an eRA Commons account; hyperlinks to view/edit/delete; Active PI accounts have 'delegate PI authority'. 'All' returns all statuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing pending status information
rubrics_metrics.description: For Pending accounts, administrators can view whether status is Pending PI Review or Pending NIH Review and may resend PI verification email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pending PI Review indicates PI hasn't replied to verification email; option to resend notification. Pending NIH Review indicates NIH has not yet completed validation. Access via Status hyperlink in query results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating affiliations for users
rubrics_metrics.description: Extramural Administrators can create institutional affiliations for existing eRA Commons users with roles of PI or IAR via Create Affiliation or query list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Create Affiliation page by entering username and email and submitting. PIs must be affiliated to see their work for that institution and can have multiple affiliations. IAR users affiliated gain access to Institution Profile and Status sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing NIH Support information (PI identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Support page lists NIH application information associated with a selected PI and helps identify PIs at an institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available for Active/Pending accounts with PI role and Not Affiliated PIs. Default list sorted by Budget Start Date descending; click column headings to change sort. Columns include PI name, grant number, title, grant status, budget start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available roles and role privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA Commons roles include Account Administrator (AA), Administrative Official (AO), Assistant (ASST), Extramural Administrator (SO/AA/AO), FSR, IAR, Principal Investigator (PI), and Signing Official (SO), each with defined privileges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AA can create/delete/modify accounts. AO reviews grant applications before final submission and can create AO and PI accounts. ASST has basic profile access and can be delegated PI authority. PI directs project and completes electronic grant process. SO can perform legally binding grant administration actions, submit applications, create/modify accounts and institution profiles. IAR and FSR roles indicate domain-specific access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleting accounts - effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Deleting an account removes the user's affiliation at the institution but does not remove the user's profile or works-in-progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only Extramural Administrators can delete accounts. After confirming deletion (optional comment), the affiliation is removed but the user's NIH profile and any associated works-in-progress remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing accounts - reassigning accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts may be reassigned to a different user via the Edit Account page, and reassigning updates displayed name/email/roles and notifies the old account holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select Reassign Account from dropdown, edit other info if desired, click Submit. The page refreshes and an email describing changes is sent to the account holder being edited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing account lock status
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts can be locked (preventing login) due to exceeding maximum login attempts or by manual lock; administrators can change lock status to allow access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Edit Account page, set Account Lock Status field to desired value, click Submit. An email is sent to the account holder detailing the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resetting passwords by administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrators or users can reset a password to a system-generated password which also unlocks locked accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the Login page click Reset Password, provide User ID and email; system sends new password to registered email. On next logon the user is prompted to change the password.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing account roles and emails
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrators can change the role(s) assigned to an account or update the account email via Edit Account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select new roles in Role field or edit Email field and click Submit. A notification email is sent to the account holder describing the changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing and editing institution profile (IPF) fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution profiles have assigned IPF code and fields such as preferred institution name, NGA email, policy/notification email, DUNS number, and indirect cost negotiator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View as read-only via Institution Profile | Basic or edit via Edit Institution Profile page if privileges allow. These fields are used for notices and institutional contact/data.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPF assurances and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions maintain assurances and certification fields (e.g., Human Subjects Assurance Number, Animal Welfare Assurance Number, ORI certification status) in the IPF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View or edit these assurances and certification fields in the IPF Assurances and Certifications pages when permitted; fields are used for compliance reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing institution usage metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution usage pages list metrics such as total number of accounts and total number of logins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Institution Usage page to view aggregate usage statistics for institutional administration and monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining organizational hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions can edit, add, and deactivate hierarchy components such as departments/divisions/schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Manage Organization Hierarchy pages to edit components, add new hierarchy components (Create New Department/Division/School pages), and deactivate components when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing personal profile information
rubrics_metrics.description: Users can edit personal profile elements including employment, degrees, publications, contact information, and delegate/revoke personal profile edit authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Personal Profile (PPF) pages to add/edit employment records (with Start/End dates), degree information, publications (NLM accession number optional), and to delegate or revoke edit rights for others to edit the PPF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifying NIH Support (PI verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs must verify NIH-maintained information about their grant participation, committee involvement, and training appointments when creating accounts or via the Accounts tab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Verify NIH Support page via email verification link or Administration | Accounts | Verify NIH Support. Review entries and select Correct or Incorrect per item. To add NIH support, click Add NIH Support, enter grant number (Serial Number is required), search and Add Grant, add comments if desired, and click Complete Account Request to notify NIH. New PI accounts are activated after this step (approx. two business days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-based visibility for Status section
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to the Status section and the scope of grant/proposal visibility depend on user role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing Officials (SOs) can search proposals and Type 5 progress reports for all PIs within their institution. PIs can view only their own proposals and Type 5 reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant number structure and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH grant numbers are composed of Type Code, Activity Code, Institute Code, Serial Number, Support Year, and optional Suffix Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 5 R01 HL123451-01A2. Serial Number is a unique five- or six-digit CSR-assigned number; Support Year (e.g., 01) indicates year of support. Use Understanding Grant Numbers to correctly query or identify grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Querying grant proposals - fields and defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: The Search Proposals page accepts optional query fields such as Budget Start Date Between, Grant Number, Accession Number, Grant Status, and Page Size (default 100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All query fields are optional; use any combination to perform searches. Budget Start Date Between finds proposals whose start/end dates fall within specified range. Grant Status values include Awarded, Pending, Withdrawn, Terminated, Not Funded, Returned, All.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing proposal search results - role-specific columns
rubrics_metrics.description: Search results display different columns depending on whether the query is run by a PI or an Extramural Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI view provides proposal title, institution name, grant status, and status date. Extramural Administrator view provides proposal title, PI name, grant status, and budget start date. Results include a hyperlinked grant number and Summary Links column with related documents when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status Information page sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Status Information page contains five sections: Status, Other Relevant Documents, Status History, Application Information, and Contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status lists a brief current message. Other Relevant Documents provides hyperlinks to related documents. Status History shows primary institute/center assignment and history of status messages. Application Information includes Study Section and Advisory Council info and roster link. Contacts lists SRA and Program Official contact info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Relevant Documents types and access rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Various document types (Abstract, Application, Fellowship Proposal Face Page, Financial Status Report (FSR), Notice of Grant Award (NGA), Progress Report Face Page, Summary Statement) are hyperlinked when available, with access rules depending on document type, grant status, and user role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Abstract hyperlink opens when application status is 'Awarded' and abstract exists (all users can access). Application hyperlink opens scanned application or eSNAP PDF; PIs and SOs can access when scanned/eSNAP exists. FSR hyperlink opens when an FSR exists (PIs and SOs access). NGA available when award made (all users). Summary Statement opens when application is 'Pending' (Type 5 or 8 and activity code not 'F') and has been released (PIs can access). See Table 4 for full per-document descriptions and display conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Querying and viewing Type 5 (non-competing) progress reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Type 5 progress reports can be searched with optional fields (Due Date Between, Page Size default 100) and results provide proposal title, PI name, budget period start date, due date, and linked grant number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select Status | Type 5 Reports to open the search page. Enter desired optional query info and Submit. The resulting Type 5 Progress Report Search Results page presents records in a table with hyperlinks to related documents (depending on grant status).
